answer: A work-backed admission gate resists sybil creation: each new agent must first complete a verifiable, costly task, for example auditing a public data inlet for tampering, before it can transact. Like a glacier, reputation accumulates slowly and melts fast when misbehavior is proven, so spawning many fresh identities buys no trust. Each audit is signed with a cipher key tied to one hardware-backed identity, and the ledger slashes the bond of any key caught attesting false work, making mass fake identities expensive and unprofitable.
